title: Project product description, work package description and plan contents
blurb: Explain the purpose and key contents of the project product description, the work package description and a plan, and how they link to quality and control.
question: A team manager needs to know the working hours, safety rules and techniques that apply to the work they have been given. Which management product should hold this?

teach.body: The plans practice relies on three management products. The project product description defines what the project as a whole must deliver and how it will be accepted. The plan (project, stage, team or exception) sets out how, when and at what cost products will be delivered. The work package description passes a defined piece of that work, formally, to a team manager or team member.

teach.caption: The PPD is written in SU; plans at each level as described earlier; WPDs are co-created by the PM and team manager in 'authorize a work package'.

teach.body: Formally, it describes the project's major products or outcomes and their purpose, including the user's quality expectations, the acceptance criteria and the acceptance methods for the project. It is created in starting up a project, when the project manager consults the executive, senior user and senior supplier about what the project will deliver. It is used at closure to confirm that the project product is acceptable.

teach.caption: The PPD starts the quality chain. Its expectations and criteria also feed the management approaches agreed in initiation.

teach.body: A work package description describes how one or more products will be produced and delivered. It is used to pass responsibility for work formally to a team manager or team member, and it should contain everything they need to complete the work. The project manager co-creates it with the team manager in controlling a stage; the team manager accepts it in managing product delivery.

head: Heading
What it holds
rows: How the work must be done
Limits such as hours, safety, security
teach.caption: Product descriptions for the products, interfaces and handover arrangements are also included. No benefits or quality tolerance is set in a WPD.

teach.body: Every plan, at any level, follows the same pattern. It describes the plan and its delivery approach, prerequisites, external dependencies and planning assumptions, then the monitoring and control arrangements, budgets, tolerances, product descriptions and schedule. A key heading is the work to be performed: the work in scope shown as a work breakdown structure with its associated work package descriptions.

children.edge: A team's hours and safety rules
children.label: Work package description

teach.body: At Corrin Bay Ferries, project manager Sofia Lindqvist runs a ticket-gate upgrade. In starting up, she wrote the project product description with executive Gareth Price and the senior user, setting acceptance criteria such as boarding times. In stage 2 she co-creates a work package with team manager Joel Ames: it sets the installation method, overnight working hours and port safety rules, scope, cost and time tolerances, and weekly checkpoint reports.

teach.text: A work package description's targets and tolerances cover scope, cost and time; benefits and quality tolerances are not agreed in it. And the WPD is not the project product description: the PPD covers the whole project and its acceptance, while a WPD covers one piece of work passed to a team.

items: PPD: the project's major products, user's quality expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods; created in SU; used to confirm acceptance at closure.
WPD: how products will be produced; formally passes work to a team manager; co-created in CS, accepted in MP.
WPD headings include techniques and procedures, constraints, references, scope/cost/time tolerances, reporting and agreement.
A plan includes its delivery approach, assumptions, dependencies, controls, budgets, tolerances, schedule and the work to be performed.
Together they link planning to quality (acceptance criteria, specifications) and control (tolerances, checkpoints).

summary: You can now explain the purpose and key contents of the project product description, the work package description and a plan. You can also show how they connect to quality, through acceptance criteria and specifications, and to control, through tolerances and reporting.

A.q: Which management product is used to pass responsibility for work formally to a team manager?
A.why: The work package description passes responsibility for work formally to a team manager or team member (7.5).

whyNot.0: The stage plan is the project manager's plan for the whole stage.
whyNot.1: The PPD describes the project's major products and acceptance at project level.
whyNot.3: Checkpoint reports flow back from the team manager on work package status.

A.q: Which product includes the acceptance criteria and acceptance methods for the project?
A.why: The project product description holds the user's quality expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods for the project (7.5).

whyNot.0: A WPD covers one piece of work, not the project's acceptance.
whyNot.2: The quality register records quality activities and results.
whyNot.3: The project plan shows major products, timing and cost, not the acceptance criteria.

A.q: Identify the missing words in the following sentence. In a plan, the [?] heading shows the work in scope as a work breakdown structure with its associated work package descriptions.
A.why: The 'work to be performed' heading shows the work in the plan's scope as a WBS and the associated work package descriptions (7.5).

whyNot.0: Planning assumptions record what the plan relies on being true.
whyNot.1: External dependencies record what the plan relies on from outside the project.
whyNot.2: Prerequisites are the fundamental things that must be in place for the plan to succeed.

B.q:
Which two items are headings of a work package description?
1. Techniques and procedures.
2. Constraints, such as authorized hours and safety.
3. Benefits tolerance.
4. The project's acceptance methods.
B.why: A WPD includes techniques and procedures and constraints such as authorized hours, safety and security (7.5).

whyNot.1: Statement 3 is false: benefits tolerance is not set in a work package description.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: the project's acceptance methods belong in the project product description.
whyNot.3: Both are false: benefits tolerance is not in a WPD, and acceptance methods are in the PPD.

B.q: In which process is the project product description used to confirm that the project product is acceptable?
B.why: The PPD's acceptance criteria are used in closing a project to confirm acceptance of the project product (7.5, 19).

whyNot.0: SU is where the PPD is created, not where acceptance is confirmed.
whyNot.1: In IP the PPD feeds the management approaches; acceptance comes at the end.
whyNot.2: CS controls the stage's work packages; project acceptance is confirmed in closing.

B.q: How often should a team manager produce checkpoint reports?
options: At the frequency set in the work package description
At the frequency set in the project product description
At the end of every management stage
When the project board requests a highlight report
B.why: Checkpoint reports are produced at the frequency defined in the work package description (7.5, 11.2).

whyNot.1: The PPD covers the project's products and acceptance, not reporting frequency.
whyNot.2: End-of-stage reporting is the project manager's end stage report.
whyNot.3: Highlight reports go from the PM to the board at intervals the board sets.

C.q: In which process, and during which activity, is the project product description created?
options: Initiating a project; prepare the project plan
Starting up a project; assemble the project brief
Initiating a project; agree the management approaches
Starting up a project; prepare the outline business case
C.why: The PPD is created in starting up a project during 'prepare the outline business case', when the PM consults the senior user, senior supplier and executive (13.4.3).

whyNot.0: The project plan is prepared in IP using the PPD, which already exists from SU.
whyNot.1: The project brief draws on the PPD; the PPD itself is created earlier, with the outline business case.
whyNot.2: In IP the PPD's expectations feed the management approaches; the PPD is not created there.

C.q: The users' quality and sustainability expectations are recorded in one product and then used in an initiation activity. Which product and which activity?
options: Project brief; establish the board's project controls
Work package description; prepare the full business case
Project product description; agree the management approaches
Quality register; agree the project's tailoring requirements
C.why: The users' quality and sustainability expectations in the PPD feed 'agree the management approaches' in initiating a project (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: The brief draws on the PPD, but the expectations are held in the PPD and used to agree the approaches.
whyNot.1: WPDs are created in CS for individual packages of work, after initiation.
whyNot.3: The quality register records quality activities and results, not expectations.

C.q: Which work package description heading records its initial authorization and final completion?
C.why: The 'agreement' heading records the initial authorization of the work package and its final completion (7.5).

whyNot.0: References point to applicable higher-level plans.
whyNot.1: Constraints set limits such as authorized hours, safety and security.
whyNot.3: Interfaces identify the people or products the work must link with.

reteach.title: Brief, contract, job sheet
reteach.question: A homeowner's wish list, a builder's programme and a subcontractor's job sheet all describe the same extension. Which PRINCE2 product is each like?

blocks.h: Three views of the same work
blocks.body: The wish list says what the finished extension must be and how the homeowner will judge it: the project product description. The builder's programme sets out what is built when and at what cost: the plan. The electrician's job sheet says exactly what to do, how, within which hours and safety rules, and how to report back: the work package description.

blocks.text: Acceptance criteria for the whole project: PPD. Hours, safety and techniques for one team's work: WPD.

explain.body: Describes the project's major products or outcomes, the user's quality expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods.

test.q: What is the purpose of the project product description?
options: To set the work package tolerances for each team
To describe the major products and their acceptance
To record the result of each quality control activity
To show the sequence in which products are developed
test.why: The PPD describes the project's major products, quality expectations, acceptance criteria and acceptance methods (7.5).

whyNot.0: Work package tolerances are set in work package descriptions.
whyNot.2: Quality control results go in the quality register.
whyNot.3: Sequence is shown in the product flow diagram.

explain.body: Describes how one or more products will be produced and delivered, and formally passes the work to a team manager or team member.

steps.label: Co-created
steps.sub: PM and TM, controlling a stage

test.q: Which statement about a work package description is correct?
options: It is written in SU for the whole project
It sets the stage tolerances for the board
It describes how products will be produced and delivered
It records lessons from the work once it is complete
test.why: A WPD describes how one or more products will be produced and delivered and passes responsibility for the work formally (7.5).

whyNot.0: WPDs are created in controlling a stage for individual packages of work.
whyNot.1: Stage tolerances are set by the board; the WPD holds work package tolerances.
whyNot.3: Lessons go in the lessons log and lessons reports.

explain.body: A plan covers its description, delivery approach, prerequisites, dependencies, assumptions, controls, budgets, tolerances, product descriptions, schedule and the work to be performed.

test.q: Which is a heading found in a plan?
test.why: Planning assumptions are among a plan's contents, alongside dependencies, controls, budgets, tolerances and the schedule (7.5).

whyNot.0: Acceptance methods for the project are held in the project product description.
whyNot.2: Risk appetite is the business's attitude to risk, described with risk management, not a plan heading.
whyNot.3: The lessons log is part of the project log, not a heading in a plan.

explain.body: Acceptance criteria and quality specifications connect planning to quality. Tolerances and reporting arrangements in plans and WPDs connect it to control.

test.q: Which content of a work package description most directly supports control by the project manager?
test.why: The WPD's targets and tolerances (scope, cost and time) set the limits within which the team manager works and when issues must be raised with the PM (7.5, 11.2.1).

whyNot.1: Acceptance methods for the project are in the PPD.
whyNot.2: Benefits are described in the business case, not the WPD.
whyNot.3: The user's quality expectations are in the PPD.
